key_insight: Property-guided diffusion can steer crystal generation toward target properties while also shifting outputs toward higher-symmetry, more physically plausible structures.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable inverse-design workflow for discovering candidate magnetic and hard crystalline materials with controllable properties for computational materials engineering.
method: Start from the lightweight DiffCrysGen diffusion model and fine-tune it with parameter-efficient adapters.
Use classifier-free guidance (CFG) to condition generation on multiple targets, including formation energy, magnetization, and Vickers hardness.
Filter candidates with geometric prescreening and MLIP-based relaxation plus thermodynamic, dynamical, and property checks.
evidence_signal: Across broad CFG strengths, the model better matched target property distributions, and the validation workflow found stable magnetic and mechanically hard materials with success rates of 12.3% and 3.9%.
watch_item: Higher guidance can improve target matching but may also bias symmetry and does not guarantee physical viability, so downstream validation remains essential.
paper_title: Property-Guided Diffusion for Inverse Design of Crystalline Materials
